subject.title: fix(telegram): Allow multi-agent ACP bindings within same account

question: For one Telegram account and topic, should a different ACP session key explicitly hand off ownership to the latest session, or should multiple active bindings coexist?
rationale: The PR claims independent multi-agent bindings, but the current storage and routing model resolves one record per account/topic, so true coexistence needs routing and delivery semantics beyond a mechanical conflict-check edit.

options.title: Treat Same-Account Rebind As Handoff
options.body: Keep one binding per account/topic, allow same-account replacement, and update the PR text, tests, and proof to match last-writer-wins behavior.

options.title: Design Multiple Active Bindings
options.body: Pause this branch until maintainers define how inbound routing, native commands, status, and completion delivery choose among several session keys for one topic.

options.title: Keep The Current Fence
options.body: Close or supersede this branch if maintainers do not want same-account topic ownership changes in Telegram ACP bindings now.

recommendation.title: Treat Same-Account Rebind As Handoff
recommendation.body: Keep one binding per account/topic, allow same-account replacement, and update the PR text, tests, and proof to match last-writer-wins behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the persistent ACP binding behavior introduced and merged through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/34873.
